clues.text: This town lies in the north of the land, on the banks of the Sava. It rests at the south foot of a great hill slope just by the town.
clues.narrowing: Puts the player on the Sava in northern south-eastern Europe.

source.quote: It is in the north of the country, along the Sava River, at the southern slopes of the Medvednica mountain.

clues.text: This town has four clear times of year, each one set far from the rest. Spring, summer, fall, and winter all come in turn here each year.
clues.narrowing: Keeps a four-season inland city with snowy winters.

clues.text: In 1991 this land broke free and stood on its own as a state. The men who made its laws then named this town its chief town.
clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to capitals proclaimed in 1991.

source.quote: After Croatia declared independence from Yugoslavia in 1991, the Parliament of the Republic of Croatia proclaimed Zagreb as the capital of the Republic of Croatia.

clues.text: Every day at noon — and it has happened since 1877! — a cannon fires from a tower in the old town to mark midday.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one capital marks noon with a daily cannon shot.

source.quote: Since 1 January 1877, the Grič cannon fires daily from the Lotrščak Tower on Grič to mark midday.

clues.text: Croatia is run from this town, where the work of state is done each day. More folk live here than in any other town in the land.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: capital and largest city of Croatia.

source.quote: Zagreb is the capital and largest city of Croatia.

reveal.blurb: Two rival towns — one of priests, one of merchants — grew side by side here for centuries before joining into one city. Every day since 1877, a cannon has fired at noon from its old tower. Zagreb is the capital of Croatia.
